approachQuestion.prompt: One range total. Given an immutable array of signed daily adjustments and one inclusive range [left, right], return the sum in that range. The array has 1 to 100,000 values, each between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000; 0 <= left <= right < length. Example: values=[4,-2,7,3], left=1, right=3 returns 8. Which method best fits this single query?
constraints: The input is already available; building an index has a cost.
The answer fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

options.text: Add the values from left through right directly, once.
options.feedback: Every value that can affect this answer is visited, and no reusable summary is needed.

options.text: Build cumulative totals for the whole array, then subtract the two totals for this query.
options.feedback: This gives the right sum, but it reads and stores the whole array before answering a single range.

options.text: Add values[left] and values[right] and return that total.
options.feedback: For values=[4,-2,7,3] and range [1,3], this returns 1 instead of 8 because it omits the middle value.

options.text: Add every value in the array, regardless of the requested endpoints.
options.feedback: It includes values outside the requested range; for [4,-2,7,3] and [1,3] it returns 12 instead of 8.

feedback.reason: Match preparation cost to how many answers will reuse it.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and auxiliary-space pair for scan-requested-range. Let k = right - left + 1. The returned number is excluded from auxiliary space.
constraints: Count each addition as constant time; the input array is not auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: The loop visits exactly the k requested entries and retains one running total. Building cumulative totals would take O(n) time and O(n) additional storage, which is not reused for another query.

methodReveal.title: Accumulate just the requested range
methodReveal.description: Start a total at zero, visit each index from left through right once, add its value, and return the total. The output is one number; the input remains unchanged.
